You receive 6 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-5 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 6 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the physics cabinet (the teachers' preparation room for physics) on the upper floor of ZŠ Sokolíkova 2 in Bratislava-Dúbravka, a typified Czechoslovak school opened in 1974. Image 2 is a real Czechoslovak physics cabinet: a wall of tall timber cupboards with glass doors next to a window; image 3 shows such timber cupboards full of physics teaching aids (meters, coils, models, boxes, books); image 4 shows a white service bench of a physics cabinet with supplies, wires and tools. Paint the furniture and the teaching aids from them, but NOT their cameras, ladders, people, plastic bags, brand names or labels. Image 5 is the real ZŠ Sokolíkova from the street side: the window looks out over the mature maples of the forecourt towards Sokolíkova street.

Brief: the physics cabinet on Thursday 15 June 1995, late afternoon: timber cupboards with models behind glass, low-voltage bench supplies, a pinned technical drawing of a bell-shaped device ("ZVON"), the old school chronicle on a small book stand. No dangerous experiments, no mains work: only low-voltage boxes and wires. The room is used and a bit worn: scuffed cupboard doors, a worn patch on the leftmost cupboard's hinge strip. The walls are one plain soft yellow colour with a slightly darker yellow-ochre dado (no murals). Warm late-afternoon sun comes in through the south-west window and falls on the window sill and the floor.

Camera: one-point perspective exactly as in the sketch. The camera stands at the door end of the room about 2.2 m high and looks straight at the back wall, which is parallel to the picture; vertical lines stay vertical; the horizon is at y 352. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the back wall from x 300 to x 1620, its floor line at y 792 and its top edge at y 232; the left and right walls recede towards the centre with their floor lines from (300, 792) and (1620, 792) to the frame edges at y 992; the ceiling above.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: in the left wall a plain honey wooden door in a brown steel frame. The right wall has NO window: only plain painted wall with a radiator pipe and, near the front, a plain wooden door. On the back wall, left: three tall timber cupboards side by side, each with two glass doors above and two solid doors below, shelves behind the glass full of physics teaching aids (analogue meters, coils, an induction coil, small models, wooden boxes, books), rolled wall charts and a cardboard box on top; the leftmost cupboard's left hinge strip is visibly worn and scuffed. In the middle of the back wall a pinned sheet with a pencil technical drawing of a bell-shaped device (illegible notes). On the right of the back wall the old double timber casement window painted white, with a light stone sill and a white radiator under it; through the glass the sunny green crowns of the forecourt maples and, below them, a glimpse of the street and a pale panel block. In the middle of the room stands the long white service bench with drawers; on its left half two low-voltage bench power supplies with analogue meters (one grey, one yellow), red and black test wires; on its right end a small slanted wooden book stand holding the old chronicle (described below). In the right wall, near the front, another plain honey wooden door in a brown steel frame, exactly like the left door. Grey-green worn linoleum floor. A plain fluorescent fitting on the white ceiling.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 1050-1210, y 585-690 of the 1920x1080 frame (55-63 % from the left, 54-64 % from the top): the old leather-bound school chronicle lying open on a small slanted wooden book stand on the right end of the white bench - a book of normal size, not a giant one; its pages full of tiny illegible handwriting, no title, no readable word.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 565-677, y 408-514 of the 1920x1080 frame (29-35 % from the left, 38-48 % from the top): a big optical model of a human eye (a white eyeball the size of a football with a brown iris and a dark pupil, on a small stand) on the shelf behind the glass of the middle cupboard.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 1205-1345, y 565-623 of the 1920x1080 frame (63-70 % from the left, 52-58 % from the top): a small clear triangular glass prism standing on the sunny window sill, throwing a little rainbow streak of colours onto the sill beside it.
NPC zone at x 385-495, y 476-886 of the 1920x1080 frame (20-26 % from the left, 44-82 % from the top): an animated character sprite will stand here later, so paint only plain, uncluttered background in it - no person, no figure, no silhouette, no clothes on hooks that read as a person. The character's feet stand on the floor at y 886. (Jana, a young woman, will stand there in front of the leftmost cupboard.)
The door in the left wall is the area of the layout sketch at x 55-190, y 395-955 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-10 % from the left, 37-88 % from the top). The door in the right wall is the area of the layout sketch at x 1730-1865, y 395-955 of the 1920x1080 frame (90-97 % from the left, 37-88 % from the top).

Walkable floor: the band at x 15-1905, y 830-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (1-99 % from the left, 77-94 % from the top) is the open grey-green linoleum floor in front of the cupboards, in front of the bench and by both doors - one continuous flat floor with no step, no rug, no change of level, and nothing standing on it: no chairs, no lectern, no stand, no boxes, no bins, no cables, no furniture in the foreground. Only light and shadows.

Fiction rules: the cabinet details are invented. No brand names or logos on the devices (no TESLA), no readable labels, no posters with text, no names. Any paper shows only illegible scribbles, no digits. No people, no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
